task.title: Native confirmation failure root-caused (401-refresh retry has no resilience); fix candidate aa165ca9 prepared and reviewed

result.summary: Superseding the prior report's incorrect 'maybe just Refresh Review' theory, which the Founder explicitly disproved by confirming the real confirm action was used and failed identically. Found decisive server-side evidence: a 401 ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRED rejection followed 190ms later by a successful token refresh, and then total silence -- confirmed definitively by a direct, bounded, read-only query of the physiqueos.command_receipts table showing ZERO rows, ever, for workout-reconciliation.resolve.v1 for this owner, and only automatic HealthKit ingestion receipts (instant-completing) in the surrounding two hours. This proves the confirm request never reached the point of being durably tracked server-side at all, ruling out any server-side idempotency/concurrency/stuck-processing defect with certainty. Root cause: Native's submitCommand gives a write command's post-401-refresh retry exactly one attempt; if that single retry hits its own independent transport failure, the write is silently lost with a generic 'could not be verified' message and no further attempt. Prepared an isolated, minimal fix (aa165ca9, based on the efcb8574 lineage) giving that retry one bounded extra attempt on a transport failure, reusing the same idempotency key (verified safe by directly reading the server's atomic ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING command-receipt insert and its per-owner advisory-lock serialization). New regression test proven RED on the original code, GREEN with the fix; full FounderServerAPITests suite 202/202 passing; independent fresh-context review returned APPROVE WITH NOTES, with all residual server-side safety questions it raised subsequently confirmed safe by direct code reading. A secondary, lower-priority code-quality gap was also found (a .pending command outcome is collapsed into the same generic error as a raw transport failure in this one call site, unlike the established pattern elsewhere in the codebase) -- not the cause of this incident, flagged as a follow-up. The Founder's notification requirement is retained unchanged from the prior report. Native is now implicated: aa165ca9 is recommended as the new Build61 candidate in place of plain efcb8574. Not deployed, not uploaded, no device operated, Founder not asked to retry.

tests.summary: New regression test reproduces the exact production sequence (401 -> refresh -> first retry drops -> second retry succeeds); proven RED on the original single-retry code, GREEN with the fix. Full FounderServerAPITests.swift suite: 202/202 passing, no regressions, iPhone 17 Pro simulator.

review.summary: Fresh-context adversarial review independently confirmed the retry behavior against both original and fixed source, independently verified refreshAccessToken's single-flight coalescing has no race, independently ran the full suite (202/202) and reproduced RED/GREEN itself, confirmed the worktree left clean. Flagged one residual assumption (server-side concurrent-idempotency-key safety) that this report subsequently confirmed directly by reading the server's own command-receipt insert and advisory-lock code -- genuinely safe, not just assumed.

zero_write_audit.summary: Bounded REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY transaction with verified transaction_read_only=on and explicit ROLLBACK, extended this task to a direct parameterized query of physiqueos.command_receipts (owner-scoped, same read-only contract) -- the decisive evidence that zero receipts of any status exist for this command, ever.

decisions_required: Authorize Native work on the aa165ca9-based lineage (or a further-reviewed descendant) whenever Founder is ready -- this both closes the retry-resilience gap and, per the retained requirement, is the natural place to add the proposed reconciliation-review notification.
No decision needed on retrying the Sep24 Strength confirmation in this task -- explicitly not requested, per the Founder's instruction.
unexpected_findings: A direct query of physiqueos.command_receipts -- a table this lane had not previously queried directly -- proved decisively, not just inferentially, that the failed confirm command never reached the server's command-processing layer at all. This is a genuinely useful new diagnostic technique for this lane: when request-level logs show ambiguous silence, the receipt table itself gives a definitive yes/no on whether the server ever durably engaged with a specific write attempt.

The codebase already has an established, correct pattern for handling a command's '.pending' outcome (HealthKitServerUploader.swift, ProductionEvidenceIntakePipeline.swift) that EvidenceReviewAPI.swift's resolveWorkoutReconciliation does not follow -- a real, independent code-quality gap, though not the cause of this specific incident.
backlog: Deploy/release the aa165ca9-based Native fix whenever Native work on Build61 is authorized.
Implement the proposed WorkoutReconciliationReviewReadyNotifier (from the prior report) on the same lineage -- no server change needed.
Optional, lower priority: harden resolveWorkoutReconciliation's handling of a .pending outcome to match the established pattern elsewhere in the codebase.
Optional, lower priority (carried from earlier reports): a scheduled, ingestion-independent catch-up sweep for Strength-candidate reassessment; improve Native's general error-classification clarity.
recommended_next_step: Founder authorizes Native work on the aa165ca9 lineage whenever ready, bundling the retry-resilience fix and the reconciliation-review notification feature together as the next Build61 preparation.
